question.problem:
Consider the matrices

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & 6\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & -7 & 6\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & -3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -6 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

I. $AB=BA={I}_{4}$

II. $AC=CA={I}_{4}$

III. $B={A}^{-1}$

current_example.problem:
Using the method of direct verification, determine whether the matrix $B$ is the inverse of $A,$ where
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14285500/assets/267bbc7c8f4410097b4b8127e1be410587ed93cd675b0cf627dbd1e171e4b943.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
First, we  check whether $AB = BA = I_3.$

Computing $AB,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{3}.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Likewise, computing $BA,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}BA & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{3}.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $B = A^{-1}.$
